title: The Four Seasons: Spring (Allegro)
stylisticClue: Bouncy Venetian ritornello strings alternating with bird-call solo violin episodes and harpsichord continuo.
funFact: Vivaldi published this violin concerto alongside a matching sonnet describing spring birdsong, babbling brooks, and a sudden afternoon thunderstorm.

title: Orchestral Suite No. 3: Air on the G String
stylisticClue: Serene sustained first-violin cantabile gliding over a walking pizzicato-like basso continuo.
spotifyQuery: Bach Orchestral Suite No 3 BWV 1068 Air
funFact: Its famous nickname comes from an 1871 arrangement by violinist August Wilhelmj, who shifted the melody so it could be played on one string.

title: Canon in D major
stylisticClue: Two-bar descending bass ostinato repeated twenty-eight times beneath three interlocking violin voices.
funFact: Nearly forgotten for centuries, this Baroque wedding favorite only became a global sensation after a French chamber orchestra recorded it in 1968.

title: Messiah: Hallelujah Chorus
stylisticClue: Jubilant choral homophony punctuated by Baroque trumpets, timpani, and contrapuntal fugal entries.
funFact: Handel composed the entire two-and-a-half-hour Messiah oratorio in a frantic 24-day burst of inspiration, reportedly barely stopping to eat or sleep.

title: Eine kleine Nachtmusik (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Crisp Mannheim-rocket arpeggio opening in G major for chamber strings.
funFact: Mozart entered this beloved serenade into his personal catalog in 1787, yet no one knows who commissioned it or if he ever heard it.

title: Symphony No. 5 in C minor (I. Allegro con brio)
stylisticClue: Obsessive four-note rhythmic cell hammered across the entire orchestra with relentless motivic development.
spotifyQuery: Beethoven Symphony No 5 Op 67 Allegro con brio
funFact: Facing worsening deafness, Beethoven poured his defiance into this symphony's famous four-note opening, later used as a BBC victory signal in World War II.

title: Für Elise (Bagatelle in A minor)
stylisticClue: Alternating E and D-sharp semitone turn opening into a gentle broken-chord A-minor rondo.
funFact: This piano favorite wasn't published until 40 years after Beethoven's death, and historians still debate which woman's name he scribbled on the lost manuscript.

title: Piano Sonata No. 11: Rondo alla Turca
stylisticClue: Playful Janissary-band piano imitation with crisp grace-note octaves and A-major march refrain.
spotifyQuery: Mozart Piano Sonata No 11 K 331 Rondo alla Turca
funFact: Mozart wrote this lively finale in the exotic 'Turkish' style, mimicking the clashing cymbals and marching drums of Ottoman military bands popular in Vienna.

title: Carmen: Votre toast (Toreador Song)
stylisticClue: Swaggering Spanish-inflected orchestral march building into an unmistakable heroic refrain.
spotifyQuery: Bizet Carmen Toreador Song Votre toast
funFact: Bizet added this swaggering bullfighter's song late in rehearsals to give the baritone a showstopper, though he cynically dismissed it as 'trash.'

title: The Nutcracker: Waltz of the Flowers
stylisticClue: Sweeping harp cadenza launching into lush Russian French-horn phrasing and crystalline orchestral color.
funFact: Though The Nutcracker is now a holiday staple, Tchaikovsky disliked working on the ballet and worried the music was far worse than Sleeping Beauty.

title: Peer Gynt: In the Hall of the Mountain King
stylisticClue: Creeping pizzicato bassoons and low strings accelerating into a crashing orchestral frenzy.
spotifyQuery: Grieg Peer Gynt In the Hall of the Mountain King
funFact: Grieg hated writing this famous troll-chase music for Ibsen's play, joking in a letter that it literally smelled of cowpats.

title: The Blue Danube Waltz
stylisticClue: Shimmering tremolos in the strings leading into a buoyant three-beat A-major arpeggio melody.
spotifyQuery: Johann Strauss II Blue Danube Waltz Op 314
funFact: Written as a choral piece to lift Viennese spirits after a war defeat, this waltz flopped at its premiere before its orchestral version conquered the world.

title: Deux Arabesques: No. 1 in E major
stylisticClue: Rippling triplets against duplets in a sunlit, flowing harp-like piano texture.
spotifyQuery: Debussy Arabesque No 1 in E major
funFact: Inspired by swirling curved lines in art and nature, the 26-year-old Debussy wrote this dreamy piano piece just as Art Nouveau swept Paris.

title: Gymnopédie No. 1
stylisticClue: Sparse, hypnotic 3/4 rocking major-seventh chords beneath a slow, wistful treble melody.
funFact: Satie named these tranquil piano pieces after an ancient Spartan festival of naked youths, while working as a bohemian cabaret pianist in Paris.

title: Pavane pour une infante défunte
stylisticClue: Nostalgic solo French horn intoning a dignified Spanish court dance over pizzicato strings and harp.
spotifyQuery: Ravel Pavane pour une infante defunte orchestra
funFact: Ravel chose the poetic title 'Pavane for a Dead Princess' simply because he loved how the French words sounded together, not to mourn anyone real.

title: Préludes Book I: La fille aux cheveux de lin
stylisticClue: Pentatonic G-flat major opening phrase unfolding with gentle, folk-like warmth and soft parallel chords.
spotifyQuery: Debussy La fille aux cheveux de lin
funFact: Debussy named this gentle prelude after a French poem set in Scotland, picturing a fair-haired girl singing among flowering clover in the summer morning.

title: Romeo and Juliet: Dance of the Knights
stylisticClue: Heavy, menacing low-brass and string stomps with angular Russian harmonic twists.
spotifyQuery: Prokofiev Dance of the Knights Romeo and Juliet
funFact: Soviet officials initially rejected Prokofiev's Romeo and Juliet ballet as 'undanceable,' and his original score even gave the doomed lovers a happy ending.

title: Carmina Burana: O Fortuna
stylisticClue: Thunderous percussion and full choir chanting medieval Latin over relentless driving ostinatos.
spotifyQuery: Carl Orff Carmina Burana O Fortuna
funFact: Orff discovered the medieval Latin text for this thunderous chorus in an 1847 book of poems written by wandering 13th-century students and monks.

title: Rhapsody in Blue
stylisticClue: Iconic solo clarinet trill and upward glissando into blues-inflected symphonic swing.
funFact: Gershwin forgot he had promised to write a jazz concerto until reading a newspaper ad, then finished the masterpiece in roughly three weeks.

title: The Planets: Jupiter, the Bringer of Jollity
stylisticClue: Buoyant brass fanfares and swirling strings giving way to a sweeping, noble British hymn tune.
funFact: Holst based his Planets suite on astrology rather than astronomy, portraying Jupiter not as a giant gas planet, but as the bringer of good cheer.

title: Toccata and Fugue in D minor
stylisticClue: Dramatic solo pipe organ rhetoric followed by tight four-voice Baroque counterpoint.
spotifyQuery: Bach Toccata and Fugue in D minor BWV 565
funFact: Bach's dramatic organ showpiece went largely forgotten for over a century until Felix Mendelssohn helped revive it in the 1840s.

title: The Four Seasons: Summer (III. Presto)
stylisticClue: Furious descending string scales depicting a violent Italian summer hailstorm.
funFact: Vivaldi printed vivid sonnets alongside the score; Summer's furious finale depicts a violent thunderstorm flattening the farmers' crops.

title: Brandenburg Concerto No. 3 in G major (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Nine-part string ensemble tossing energetic sixteenth-note motifs in tight rhythmic interlock.
funFact: Bach sent this concerto in a 1721 presentation set to a German nobleman, who apparently never thanked him, paid him, or had the score performed.

title: Adagio in G minor (attr. Albinoni / Giazotto)
stylisticClue: Plodding organ and pizzicato bass supporting mournful, soaring string suspensions.
funFact: Although credited to Baroque composer Albinoni, this famous tragic piece was actually composed by Italian musicologist Remo Giazotto and published in 1958.

title: Symphony No. 40 in G minor (I. Molto allegro)
stylisticClue: Restless half-step sighing motif over pulsing violas—Classical-era Sturm und Drang minor-key urgency.
spotifyQuery: Mozart Symphony No 40 K 550 Molto allegro
funFact: Mozart completed this stormy, urgent symphony in just a few weeks during the summer of 1788, alongside two other symphonic masterpieces.

title: Piano Sonata No. 14 'Moonlight' (I. Adagio sostenuto)
stylisticClue: Hushed C-sharp minor triplet ostinato under a brooding, bell-like soprano line.
spotifyQuery: Beethoven Moonlight Sonata Op 27 No 2 Adagio sostenuto
funFact: Beethoven didn't name it 'Moonlight'—a German poet coined the nickname five years after the composer's death, comparing it to moonlit lake waves.

title: Symphony No. 94 'Surprise' (II. Andante)
stylisticClue: Delicate tiptoeing C-major string theme shattered by a sudden fortissimo orchestral crash.
funFact: Despite the popular myth about waking sleepy listeners, Haydn added this sudden, thunderous chord simply to startle London audiences and outshine rival concerts.

title: Piano Concerto No. 21 in C major (II. Andante)
stylisticClue: Muted violins with triplet accompaniment cradling a serene, singing piano cantabile.
spotifyQuery: Mozart Piano Concerto No 21 K 467 Andante
funFact: This dreamy movement gained a modern nickname after starring in the 1967 Swedish film Elvira Madigan, sparking a classical-music craze.

title: Nocturne in E-flat major
stylisticClue: Bel canto vocal cantilena in the right hand with ornamental fioritura over a steady waltz-like bass.
funFact: Chopin wrote this dreamy, singing piano piece around age twenty, shortly before leaving his Polish homeland for Paris forever.

title: Swan Lake: Scene (Moderato)
stylisticClue: Plaintive solo oboe gliding over shimmering harp arpeggios and tremolo strings before brass swells.
funFact: At its 1877 Moscow premiere, critics panned Swan Lake as 'too noisy' and the choreography as dull; fame came only after Tchaikovsky's death.

title: William Tell Overture (Finale)
stylisticClue: Galloping brass bugle call launching into a breathless, unstoppable orchestral cavalry charge.
funFact: Written for Rossini's final opera in 1829, this galloping finale later became iconic as the theme music for The Lone Ranger.

title: Enigma Variations: IX. Nimrod
stylisticClue: Whispered E-flat major strings rising slowly to a radiant, brass-crowned orchestral climax.
funFact: Elgar wrote 'Nimrod' to honor his close friend and publisher August Jaeger, whose surname means 'hunter' in German—just like the biblical Nimrod.

title: Clair de lune (Suite bergamasque)
stylisticClue: Floating ninth chords, blurred pedal resonance, and gentle 9/8 rubato avoiding functional cadences.
funFact: Debussy first called this gentle piano piece 'Promenade sentimentale,' only renaming it 'Clair de lune' after a Paul Verlaine poem years later.

title: Boléro
stylisticClue: Unchanging ostinato snare drum and two-part modal melody passed instrument by instrument.
funFact: Ravel described Boléro as a seventeen-minute orchestral crescendo with 'no music in it'—yet it became his most famous work worldwide.

title: Prélude à l'après-midi d'un faune
stylisticClue: Languid solo flute tracing a chromatic tritone curve answered by shimmering harp glissandi and horns.
spotifyQuery: Debussy Prelude a l'apres-midi d'un faune
funFact: When Vaslav Nijinsky choreographed this sensual piece into a 1912 ballet, its bold movements shocked Parisian audiences into a near-riot.

title: The Sorcerer's Apprentice
stylisticClue: Bouncy bassoon motif marching steadily forward as orchestral magic multiplies out of control.
funFact: Inspired by a Goethe poem, Dukas's magical tale of out-of-control broomsticks became world-famous thanks to Mickey Mouse in Disney's Fantasia.

title: Adagio for Strings
stylisticClue: Stepwise B-flat minor string arch climbing relentlessly to an agonizing high-register apex.
spotifyQuery: Samuel Barber Adagio for Strings Op 11
funFact: Originally written as part of a string quartet, this deeply moving piece later became America's unofficial music of mourning for presidents and tragedies.

title: Fanfare for the Common Man
stylisticClue: Booming bass drum, tam-tam, and wide-open fourths and fifths in unison trumpets and horns.
spotifyQuery: Copland Fanfare for the Common Man
funFact: Written to honor everyday Americans during World War II, Copland's brass fanfare was even adapted into a hit rock single by Emerson, Lake & Palmer.

title: Gayane: Sabre Dance
stylisticClue: Driving xylophone and string ostinato whipped by brass glissandi and Armenian folk chromaticism.
funFact: Khachaturian dashed off this frenzied dance in a single evening right before his ballet's premiere, never guessing it would become a jukebox hit.

title: Suite for Variety Orchestra: Waltz No. 2
stylisticClue: Wry alto saxophone and muted trombone melody swinging with bittersweet Soviet cabaret charm.
spotifyQuery: Shostakovich Waltz No 2 Suite for Variety Orchestra
funFact: Often mislabeled as 'Jazz Suite No. 2,' this wistful waltz actually comes from a later medley Shostakovich assembled from his film scores.

title: Water Music Suite No. 2: Alla Hornpipe
stylisticClue: Festive outdoor antiphony trading bright natural horns and trumpets against oboe-led strings.
funFact: Handel wrote Water Music for King George I's lavish 1717 River Thames boat party, where 50 musicians played from a barge floating alongside the royal vessel.

title: Cello Suite No. 1 in G major (I. Prélude)
stylisticClue: Rolling broken-chord arpeggios for solo cello outlining implied Baroque harmony.
spotifyQuery: Bach Cello Suite No 1 BWV 1007 Prelude
funFact: Bach's cello suites were largely forgotten for over a century until teenage cellist Pablo Casals stumbled upon a yellowed copy in a Barcelona thrift shop in 1890.

title: King Arthur: What Power Art Thou (Cold Song)
stylisticClue: Shivering repeated string chords rising chromatically beneath a trembling bass-baritone.
spotifyQuery: Purcell King Arthur Cold Song What Power Art Thou
funFact: In this 1691 opera aria, Purcell makes the singer stutter and shiver on repeated notes to portray the Spirit of Winter waking up in the freezing cold.

title: Brandenburg Concerto No. 2 in F major (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Clarino Baroque trumpet soaring above recorder, oboe, and solo violin concertino.
funFact: Bach sent the Brandenburg Concertos as a job application to a German margrave, who apparently never paid him, thanked him, or even had the pieces performed.

title: Symphony No. 3 'Eroica' (I. Allegro con brio)
stylisticClue: Two hammer-blow E-flat chords launching a cello theme jolted by an unexpected C-sharp.
spotifyQuery: Beethoven Symphony No 3 Eroica Allegro con brio
funFact: Beethoven originally dedicated his Third Symphony to Napoleon, but furiously scratched the name out after hearing that Napoleon had crowned himself emperor.

title: Symphony No. 41 'Jupiter' (IV. Molto allegro)
stylisticClue: Four-note plainsong motif spun into a dazzling five-voice Classical fugato finale.
spotifyQuery: Mozart Symphony No 41 Jupiter Molto allegro
funFact: Mozart wrote this grand final symphony in the summer of 1788, and a London concert promoter later nicknamed it 'Jupiter' after the king of the Roman gods.

title: Symphony No. 104 'London' (I. Adagio — Allegro)
stylisticClue: Solemn D-minor unison call giving way to a buoyant, monothematic D-major string theme.
funFact: Written for his triumphant 1795 London concert series, this was the final symphony Haydn ever composed, capping a career that made him both rich and world-famous.

title: Clarinet Concerto in A major (II. Adagio)
stylisticClue: Warm chalumeau-register clarinet phrasing floating effortlessly over hushed string chords.
funFact: Written just two months before Mozart's death for his close friend Anton Stadler, this concerto showcased a newly invented clarinet with extra low notes.

title: Symphony No. 8 'Unfinished' (I. Allegro moderato)
stylisticClue: Brooding low-string unison followed by an oboe/clarinet cantabile over rippling sixteenth-note strings.
spotifyQuery: Schubert Symphony No 8 Unfinished Allegro moderato
funFact: Schubert finished only two movements and gave the score to a friend, who kept it hidden in a drawer until its 1865 premiere, 37 years after Schubert's death.

title: Symphony No. 3 in F major (III. Poco allegretto)
stylisticClue: Autumnal cello melody wrapped in Brahmsian cross-rhythms and warm horn sonorities.
funFact: Brahms wove his personal motto—'Free, but happy'—as a three-note musical code into this symphony, composed during a peaceful summer retreat on the Rhine.

title: Symphony No. 9 'From the New World' (II. Largo)
stylisticClue: Hushed brass chorale modulation opening onto an aching solo English horn melody.
spotifyQuery: Dvorak Symphony No 9 Largo English horn
funFact: Inspired by African American spirituals and Native American music during his stay in America, Dvořák wrote a symphony so beloved that Neil Armstrong took a recording to the Moon.

title: Symphony No. 5 (IV. Adagietto)
stylisticClue: Suspended chromatic suspensions scored purely for strings and harp with bittersweet longing.
funFact: Mahler composed this tender movement for strings and harp as a musical love letter to Alma Schindler during their whirlwind courtship, shortly before their 1902 wedding.

title: La Mer (I. De l'aube à midi sur la mer)
stylisticClue: Misty low-string swells and muted trumpet calls cresting into divided cellos and harp waves.
spotifyQuery: Debussy La Mer De l'aube a midi sur la mer
funFact: Debussy began sketching the ocean inland from memory and imagination, even choosing the famous Japanese woodblock print 'The Great Wave' for the sheet music cover.

title: Daphnis et Chloé Suite No. 2: Lever du jour
stylisticClue: Rippling flute and clarinet bird-calls over wordless chorus and glowing orchestral sunrise.
spotifyQuery: Ravel Daphnis et Chloe Lever du jour
funFact: Written for the famous Ballets Russes, Ravel's shimmering 'Daybreak' depicts sunrise over an ancient Greek meadow through rippling flutes and orchestral birdsong.

title: Pines of Rome (IV. The Pines of the Appian Way)
stylisticClue: Distant marching bass ostinato growing into a blazing Roman legion triumph with offstage brass.
spotifyQuery: Respighi Pines of Rome Pines of the Appian Way
funFact: To summon the vision of a ghostly Roman army marching at dawn, Respighi added extra offstage brass instruments that build the finale to a thunderous roar.

title: The Lark Ascending
stylisticClue: Free-meter pentatonic solo violin fluttering high above muted English modal strings.
funFact: Vaughan Williams sketched this soaring violin piece while watching warships cross the English Channel in 1914—and was briefly detained by police as a suspected spy.

title: The Firebird Suite: Finale
stylisticClue: Solo horn intoning a Russian folk tune that builds into radiant 7/4 brass triumph.
funFact: Before The Firebird, Stravinsky was virtually unknown outside Russia; its dazzling 1910 Paris premiere turned the 28-year-old composer into an overnight international star.

title: Symphony No. 1 'Classical' (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Haydn-sized orchestra playing crisp Classical scales spiked with sudden witty harmonic side-slips.
funFact: Prokofiev wrote this crisp, playful symphony during the chaos of the 1917 Russian Revolution, imagining what Haydn's music would sound like in the 20th century.

title: Symphony No. 5 in D minor (IV. Allegro non troppo)
stylisticClue: Timpani-driven march accelerating into an ambiguous, hammered D-major brass peroration.
spotifyQuery: Shostakovich Symphony No 5 Op 47 Allegro non troppo
funFact: After Stalin's regime publicly condemned his earlier work, Shostakovich unveiled this symphony in 1937 and earned a 30-minute standing ovation that likely saved his life.

title: Appalachian Spring (Simple Gifts)
stylisticClue: Clear solo clarinet presenting a Shaker melody followed by bright, open-voiced variations.
funFact: Originally scored for just 13 players, the ballet had no name until choreographer Martha Graham borrowed 'Appalachian Spring' from a poem right before opening night.

title: Passacaglia and Fugue in C minor
stylisticClue: Eight-measure pedal ostinato climbing through twenty polyphonic variations into a double fugue.
spotifyQuery: Bach Passacaglia and Fugue in C minor BWV 582
funFact: Bach borrowed part of the opening melody from French organist André Raison, repeating that eight-bar tune twenty times beneath ever-richer organ fireworks.

title: Vespro della Beata Vergine: Deus in adjutorium
stylisticClue: Blazing brass and string fanfare framing choral falsobordone chanting on a single chord.
funFact: Monteverdi opened this sacred church masterpiece with a flashy fanfare recycled straight from his own opera Orfeo, thrilling listeners by bringing theater into the cathedral.

title: Concerto Grosso in G minor 'Christmas Concerto'
stylisticClue: Two solo violins and cello trading luminous suspensions against full Baroque ripieno strings.
spotifyQuery: Corelli Concerto Grosso Op 6 No 8 Christmas
funFact: Corelli inscribed this concerto 'written for Christmas Eve,' closing with a gentle pastoral dance meant to evoke Italian shepherds playing bagpipes in the hills.

title: Keyboard Sonata in D minor
stylisticClue: Machine-gun repeated notes and Spanish guitar-like acciaccaturas crackling across the keyboard.
spotifyQuery: Scarlatti Sonata in D minor K 141
funFact: Having spent decades serving the Spanish royal court in Madrid, Scarlatti packed this fiery keyboard sonata with rapid repeated notes imitating a strumming Spanish guitar.

title: Serenade No. 10 'Gran Partita' (III. Adagio)
stylisticClue: Pulsing accompaniment beneath trading solos for oboe, clarinet, and velvety basset horns.
funFact: Featured memorably in the film Amadeus, this glowing slow movement was scored for twelve wind instruments and a double bass instead of a standard orchestra.

title: String Quartet in D minor 'Fifths' (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Stark falling fifths in the first violin answered by terse contrapuntal wit and canonic drive.
spotifyQuery: Haydn String Quartet Op 76 No 2 Fifths Allegro
funFact: Named for the bold leaping intervals at its start, this quartet also features a quirky 'Witches' Minuet' where two pairs of strings chase each other in a round.

title: String Quartet No. 7 'Razumovsky' (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Broad cello melody rising over pulsing eighth-note chords into symphonic quartet scale.
spotifyQuery: Beethoven String Quartet Op 59 No 1 Allegro
funFact: Commissioned by Russia's ambassador to Vienna, Beethoven's boundary-pushing quartet so baffled musicians in 1806 that one violinist reportedly accused him of playing a practical joke.

title: Piano Concerto No. 24 in C minor (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Creeping chromatic unison theme in C minor answered by woodwind-rich tragic drama.
spotifyQuery: Mozart Piano Concerto No 24 K 491 Allegro
funFact: One of only two minor-key piano concertos Mozart ever wrote, this stormy work so awed Beethoven that he told a friend they could never match it.

title: Symphonie fantastique (III. Scène aux champs)
stylisticClue: Pastoral dialogue between offstage oboe and onstage English horn later shadowed by four-timpani thunder.
spotifyQuery: Berlioz Symphonie fantastique Scene aux champs
funFact: Written during Berlioz's obsessive infatuation with actress Harriet Smithson, this countryside scene opens with an offstage oboe and English horn echoing like distant shepherds.

title: Symphony No. 4 in E minor (IV. Allegro energico)
stylisticClue: Eight-bar Baroque-inspired chaconne theme hammered by winds and brass across thirty symphonic variations.
spotifyQuery: Brahms Symphony No 4 Allegro energico e passionato
funFact: Brahms modeled this thunderous finale on an old Baroque pattern he found in a Bach cantata, spinning thirty dramatic variations from one stubborn eight-note theme.

title: Kreisleriana (No. 1: Äusserst bewegt)
stylisticClue: Headlong D-minor triplet turbulence colliding with tender, syncopated inner voices.
funFact: Secretly engaged to Clara Wieck, Schumann dashed off this stormy piano cycle in four days, naming it after a wild, eccentric fictional conductor from E.T.A. Hoffmann's tales.

title: Tristan und Isolde: Prelude
stylisticClue: Unresolved chromatic yearning built around the half-diminished 'Tristan chord' and rising oboe sighs.
funFact: Wagner's famous opening chord refuses to settle peacefully for over four hours until the opera's final scene, keeping listeners suspended in constant, aching longing.

title: Le Tombeau de Couperin (I. Prélude)
stylisticClue: Featherlight oboe and flute filigree spinning Baroque-inspired 12/16 ornaments with French wit.
spotifyQuery: Ravel Le Tombeau de Couperin Prelude orchestra
funFact: Ravel dedicated each movement of this sparkling suite to a friend killed in World War I, replying to critics of its brightness: 'The dead are sad enough.'

title: Jeux (Poème dansé)
stylisticClue: Kaleidoscopic orchestral wisps shifting tempo and timbre every few bars without fixed themes.
funFact: Debussy wrote this shimmering score for a Ballets Russes dance about three young people flirting while hunting a lost tennis ball—premiering right before The Rite of Spring.

title: On Hearing the First Cuckoo in Spring
stylisticClue: Chromatic string harmonies cradling a Norwegian folk melody punctuated by clarinet cuckoo calls.
spotifyQuery: Delius On Hearing the First Cuckoo in Spring
funFact: Though loved as a quintessentially English nature portrait, Delius actually built this dreamy springtime miniature around a Norwegian folk song given to him by Percy Grainger.

title: Mythes: La Fontaine d'Aréthuse
stylisticClue: Ecstatic quarter-tone-like violin harmonics shimmering over bitonal piano water-ripples.
funFact: Inspired by a trip to Sicily, Szymanowski teamed up with violinist Paweł Kochański to invent shimmering, watery effects depicting a Greek nymph turning into a fountain.

title: Symphony 'Mathis der Maler' (I. Engelkonzert)
stylisticClue: Trombones intoning a German folk chorale amid quartal brass harmonies and contrapuntal strings.
funFact: Before finishing his opera on Renaissance painter Matthias Grünewald, Hindemith turned parts of it into this symphony depicting angels playing music around the Nativity.

title: Sinfonietta (I. Fanfare: Allegretto)
stylisticClue: Twelve trumpets, bass trumpets, and tenor tubas blasting terse Moravian ostinatos.
funFact: Inspired by an outdoor military band and dedicated to the young Czechoslovak army, Janáček launches this exhilarating work with a blazing fanfare for eleven trumpets and two tenor tubas.

title: Serenade for Tenor, Horn and Strings (Prologue)
stylisticClue: Unaccompanied French horn playing natural, untempered overtones that bend eerily in twilight.
spotifyQuery: Britten Serenade for Tenor Horn and Strings Prologue
funFact: Written during World War II for Britten's partner Peter Pears and horn virtuoso Dennis Brain, the piece opens with an eerie, unvarnished horn solo.

title: Quatuor pour la fin du temps (I. Liturgie de cristal)
stylisticClue: Clarinet and violin birdsong suspended over asymmetric cello harmonics and a 29-chord piano cycle.
spotifyQuery: Messiaen Quatuor pour la fin du temps Liturgie de cristal
funFact: Messiaen composed and premiered this haunting quartet in 1941 inside a German prisoner-of-war camp, writing for the exact four instruments available among fellow prisoners.

title: The Art of Fugue: Contrapunctus I
stylisticClue: Stark D-minor triadic subject entering voice by voice in pure, austere Baroque counterpoint.
funFact: Bach wrote this monumental collection of intertwined melodies in his final years, leaving the very last piece unfinished at his death in 1750.

title: Trio Sonata No. 5 in F major (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Virtuosic twin oboes and gnarly bassoon obligato weaving eccentric Bohemian syncopations.
spotifyQuery: Zelenka Trio Sonata No 5 ZWV 181 Allegro
funFact: Written for two oboes, bassoon, and keyboard at the Dresden court, this dazzling piece pushed woodwind players to the limits of virtuosity.

title: Mystery (Rosary) Sonatas: Passacaglia in G minor
stylisticClue: Descending four-note tetrachord repeated sixty-five times in polyphonic solo violin variations.
spotifyQuery: Biber Passacaglia in G minor Guardian Angel
funFact: This lone solo violin meditation closes a cycle of fifteen Rosary sonatas, inspired by a guardian angel engraving at the end of the manuscript.

title: Les Boréades: Entrée de Polymnie
stylisticClue: Hushed, trembling French strings and bassoons floating in luminous harmonic suspension.
spotifyQuery: Rameau Les Boreades Entree de Polymnie
funFact: Rameau died in 1764 during rehearsals for this final opera, and the score sat unperformed for more than two centuries until 1964.

title: String Quartet No. 16 in E-flat major (I. Allegro ma non troppo)
stylisticClue: Chromatic octave unison opening that dissolves into daring enharmonic quartet counterpoint.
spotifyQuery: Mozart String Quartet K 428 Allegro ma non troppo
funFact: Mozart dedicated this quartet and five companions to Joseph Haydn, calling them the fruit of long and laborious effort out of deep admiration.

title: String Quartet in F minor (IV. Fuga a due soggetti)
stylisticClue: Sotto voce double fugue in F minor built on a jagged Baroque-style diminished-seventh leap.
spotifyQuery: Haydn String Quartet Op 20 No 5 Fuga
funFact: Haydn helped shape the modern string quartet by letting all four instruments share the spotlight equally, ending this intense work with a classic musical chase.

title: Piano Sonata in G minor 'Didone abbandonata' (I. Largo — Allegro)
stylisticClue: Brooding chromatic recitative giving way to stormy Beethovenian piano counterpoint.
spotifyQuery: Clementi Sonata Op 50 No 3 Didone abbandonata
funFact: Inspired by Queen Dido's tragic abandonment in Virgil's Aeneid, Clementi published this dramatic work at age sixty-nine as his final piano sonata.

title: Cello Concerto in A major (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Nervous, mercurial string syncopations and sudden dynamic shifts framing fiery solo cello runs.
spotifyQuery: CPE Bach Cello Concerto in A major Wq 172 Allegro
funFact: Johann Sebastian's second surviving son wrote this fiery concerto while serving King Frederick the Great, who famously preferred flutes over cellos.

title: String Quartet No. 14 in C-sharp minor (I. Adagio ma non troppo)
stylisticClue: Subdominant-answering opening fugue full of agonizing chromatic half-steps without pause.
spotifyQuery: Beethoven String Quartet Op 131 Adagio ma non troppo
funFact: Beethoven reportedly called this seven-movement work his greatest string quartet, and Franz Schubert asked to hear it five days before his own death in 1828.

title: Piano Sonata in B minor
stylisticClue: Mysterious Phrygian descending scales exploding into octave fury and thematic transformation.
spotifyQuery: Liszt Piano Sonata in B minor S 178
funFact: When Liszt first played this stormy half-hour masterpiece for friends in 1853, a young, exhausted Johannes Brahms famously dozed off in his chair.

title: Piano Quintet in F minor (I. Allegro non troppo)
stylisticClue: Dark unison opening in strings and piano erupting into volcanic F-minor counterpoint.
spotifyQuery: Brahms Piano Quintet Op 34 Allegro non troppo
funFact: Brahms first drafted this turbulent work as a string quintet and later as a two-piano duet before finally finding its ideal voice here.

title: Symphony No. 8 in C minor (IV. Finale: Feierlich)
stylisticClue: Galloping string ostinato beneath massive Wagner-tuba and brass chorale blocks.
funFact: Nicknamed the 'Apocalyptic,' this colossal finale took Bruckner years of anxious revisions after a conductor rejected his earlier version.

title: Gaspard de la nuit: Ondine
stylisticClue: Whispered, superhumanly fast right-hand water shimmer beneath a seductive water-nymph melody.
spotifyQuery: Ravel Gaspard de la nuit Ondine
funFact: Inspired by a prose poem about a water nymph luring a mortal to her lake, Ravel deliberately tried to make this piano piece impossibly hard.

title: Études, Book II: Pour les sonorités opposées
stylisticClue: Distant horn-like fifths layered against crystalline bell resonances in three simultaneous planes.
spotifyQuery: Debussy Etude Pour les sonorites opposees
funFact: Written during World War I while Debussy battled terminal cancer, this late piano collection served as a tribute to Frédéric Chopin.

title: Symphony No. 5 'Prometheus: The Poem of Fire'
stylisticClue: Quartal 'mystic chord' mist pierced by ecstatic solo piano trills and solo trumpet.
spotifyQuery: Scriabin Prometheus Poem of Fire Op 60
funFact: Scriabin built this cosmic symphony around a 'color organ' designed to project shifting colored lights across the concert hall in sync with the music.

title: Chamber Symphony in One Movement
stylisticClue: Opulent harp, celesta, and harmonium colorism enveloping solo winds in Viennese twilight.
funFact: Written in 1916 for the Vienna Music Academy's centenary, this shimmering work packs a full four-part symphony into one continuous movement.

title: Symphony No. 9 in D major (I. Andante comodo)
stylisticClue: Halt-stepped cello, horn, and harp heartbeat fracturing into soaring, nostalgic string polyphony.
funFact: Having left Das Lied von der Erde unnumbered to dodge the 'Curse of the Ninth,' Mahler numbered this heartbreaking farewell, which premiered after his death.

title: The Rite of Spring (Augurs of Spring)
stylisticClue: Polychordal string stomping with jagged, unpredictable accents and primitive Russian folk-inspired ostinatos.
spotifyQuery: Stravinsky Rite of Spring Augurs of Spring
funFact: Its 1913 Paris premiere sparked a famous opening-night uproar, with audience members jeering and shouting over the pounding rhythms and radical choreography.

title: Concerto for Orchestra (II. Giuoco delle coppie)
stylisticClue: Wry snareless side drum introduction followed by wind pairs marching in fixed parallel intervals.
spotifyQuery: Bartok Concerto for Orchestra Giuoco delle coppie
funFact: Commissioned while Bartók was gravely ill in New York exile, this witty movement pairs orchestral instruments two by two like a playful parade.

title: Symphony No. 10 in E minor (II. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Relentless four-minute whirlwind of biting piccolos, shrieking E-flat clarinet, and brutal snare-drum snaps.
funFact: Completed months after Joseph Stalin's death in 1953, this ferocious, galloping movement is widely regarded as a blistering musical portrait of the Soviet dictator.

title: The Four Seasons: Winter (I. Allegro non molto)
stylisticClue: Icy shivering repeated eighth-note chords broken by biting solo violin arpeggios.
spotifyQuery: Vivaldi Four Seasons Winter Allegro non molto
funFact: Vivaldi wrote icy violin effects into this concerto to match his own poem about chattering teeth, stamping feet in the snow, and slipping on ice.

title: Herz und Mund und Tat und Leben: Jesu, Joy of Man's Desiring
stylisticClue: Flowing triplet oboe and violin obbligato weaving gently around a solemn Lutheran chorale.
spotifyQuery: Bach Jesu Joy of Man's Desiring BWV 147
funFact: Written for a church service in 1723, this serene melody became famous worldwide through English pianist Myra Hess's 1926 solo piano arrangement.

title: Music for the Royal Fireworks: La Réjouissance
stylisticClue: Jubilant Baroque trumpets, horns, and timpani alternating with crisp oboe-and-bassoon choirs.
funFact: Handel wrote this joyful fanfare for a 1749 London fireworks celebration in Green Park, where misfiring rockets accidentally burned down part of the wooden pavilion.

title: Prince of Denmark's March (Trumpet Voluntary)
stylisticClue: Stately, bright solo trumpet melody marching cleanly over a crisp Baroque snare and organ.
spotifyQuery: Jeremiah Clarke Trumpet Voluntary Prince of Denmark's March
funFact: Long mistaken for a work by Henry Purcell, this regal wedding favorite was actually composed around 1700 for harpsichord by English organist Jeremiah Clarke.

title: The Well-Tempered Clavier Book I: Prelude in C major
stylisticClue: Pure, unbroken stream of five-note rising arpeggios outlining serene Baroque harmonic progressions.
spotifyQuery: Bach Prelude in C major BWV 846
funFact: Bach wrote this serene opening prelude for his eldest son's keyboard lessons, long before French composer Charles Gounod added 'Ave Maria' on top.

title: String Quintet in E major: Minuetto
stylisticClue: Delicate, courtly pizzicato accompaniment beneath a graceful, lilting solo violin minuet.
spotifyQuery: Boccherini Minuetto String Quintet Op 11 No 5
funFact: Boccherini wrote more than 100 string quintets, yet this single dainty minuet became so famous it overshadowed almost everything else he ever composed.

title: Suite de symphonies No. 1: Rondeau
stylisticClue: Regal natural trumpet fanfare alternating with brisk French string and timpani refrains.
funFact: Premiered at a Paris concert hall in 1729, this regal brass fanfare found modern fame in 1971 as the theme for PBS's Masterpiece Theatre.

title: Orchestral Suite No. 2: Badinerie
stylisticClue: Breathless, sparkling solo transverse flute leaping through playful B-minor arpeggios.
funFact: Meaning 'banter' or 'playful teasing' in French, this breathless flute showcase races along as one of the fastest solo pieces in Bach's entire catalog.

title: Symphony No. 9 'Choral' (IV. Ode to Joy Theme)
stylisticClue: Hushed low-string unison hymn blooming into triumphant full orchestra and chorus.
spotifyQuery: Beethoven Symphony No 9 Ode to Joy
funFact: Completely deaf at the 1824 premiere, Beethoven had to be gently turned around by a singer so he could see the audience cheering wildly.

title: Piano Sonata No. 16 in C major (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Limpid C-major melody over an Alberti-bass left hand breaking into crisp scale runs.
funFact: Mozart labeled this famous C-major piece a 'little piano sonata for beginners,' though its clean, exposed melodies leave pianists nowhere to hide.

title: The Magic Flute: Der Hölle Rache (Queen of the Night)
stylisticClue: Fierce D-minor string chords launching stratospheric staccato F6 soprano coloratura.
spotifyQuery: Mozart Queen of the Night Der Holle Rache
funFact: Mozart wrote this famously sky-high villain aria for his sister-in-law Josepha Hofer, whose extraordinary vocal range could hit towering notes with ease.

title: Piano Sonata No. 8 'Pathétique' (II. Adagio cantabile)
stylisticClue: Warm, hymn-like A-flat major singing melody cradled by gentle inner-voice sixteenth chords.
funFact: Beethoven's publisher suggested the dramatic title 'Pathétique' for this stormy sonata, and the composer approved—balancing it with this tender, hymn-like slow movement.

title: Symphony No. 101 'The Clock' (II. Andante)
stylisticClue: Steady staccato bassoon and pizzicato tick-tock pulsing beneath a poised violin tune.
funFact: Haydn gave this symphony a steady ticking accompaniment to delight London audiences, who nicknamed it 'The Clock' right after its 1794 premiere.

title: Così fan tutte: Overture
stylisticClue: Witty woodwind chatter and scurrying C-major strings sparkling with theatrical energy.
funFact: This sparkling comedy's 1790 Vienna run was abruptly cut short after just five performances when Emperor Joseph II died, plunging the city into mourning.

title: Symphony No. 1 in C major (I. Adagio molto — Allegro con brio)
stylisticClue: Cheeky off-tonic opening chords resolving into brisk, Haydn-inspired Classical momentum.
spotifyQuery: Beethoven Symphony No 1 Allegro con brio
funFact: At age 29, Beethoven famously opened his very first symphony with a cheeky, unexpected chord that startled proper Viennese audiences in 1800.

title: Orfeo ed Euridice: Dance of the Blessed Spirits
stylisticClue: Serene solo flute floating in pure, unadorned D-minor melancholy over muted strings.
spotifyQuery: Gluck Dance of the Blessed Spirits
funFact: Gluck added this serene flute-led underworld ballet for the 1774 Paris revision of Orfeo ed Euridice, expanding his pioneering reform opera for French audiences.

title: Piano Concerto No. 1 in B-flat minor (I. Opening)
stylisticClue: Four thunderous French-horn blasts answered by towering, crashing piano chords and sweeping strings.
funFact: Pianist Nikolai Rubinstein furiously declared this concerto 'worthless and unplayable,' so Tchaikovsky dedicated it instead to Hans von Bülow, who championed it worldwide.

title: Rigoletto: La donna è mobile
stylisticClue: Jaunty, swaggering 3/8 tenor melody punctuated by crisp pizzicato strings and brass.
spotifyQuery: Verdi Rigoletto La donna e mobile
funFact: Fearing this catchy tune would leak and be whistled across Venice before opening night, Verdi kept it secret until the final dress rehearsal.

title: Hungarian Dance No. 5 in G minor
stylisticClue: Fiery gypsy-style violin melody snapping between slow, brooding rubato and sudden prestissimo.
funFact: Brahms thought he was adapting an authentic Hungarian folk tune here, unaware it had actually been composed by Hungarian bandleader Béla Kéler.

title: A Midsummer Night's Dream: Wedding March
stylisticClue: Crisp trumpet triplets heralding a jubilant C-major processional fanfare.
funFact: Mendelssohn wrote this march at age 33 for a Shakespeare play, and it became a wedding standard after Princess Victoria used it in 1858.

title: Orpheus in the Underworld: Infernal Galop (Can-Can)
stylisticClue: Breathless, high-kicking Parisian orchestral gallop bursting with brass and cymbals.
spotifyQuery: Offenbach Orpheus in the Underworld Infernal Galop
funFact: Originally written as a spoof of ancient Greek gods behaving badly, this wild galop became the signature music of Paris's Moulin Rouge dance hall.

title: Turandot: Nessun dorma
stylisticClue: Hushed nocturnal strings swelling into an unforgettable, soaring high-B tenor triumph.
funFact: Puccini died before finishing Turandot, so at the 1926 premiere, conductor Arturo Toscanini halted the performance right where the dying composer's pen had stopped.

title: Slavonic Dance in C major
stylisticClue: Exuberant furiant cross-rhythms crashing out with festive Bohemian brass and strings.
funFact: Inspired by Brahms's Hungarian Dances, Dvořák invented original Czech-style melodies for these dances, which sold out immediately and launched his international career.

title: The Carnival of the Animals: The Swan
stylisticClue: Gliding solo cello melody drifting serenely over rippling, watery piano arpeggios.
spotifyQuery: Saint-Saens The Swan Carnival of the Animals
funFact: Saint-Saëns banned performances of Carnival of the Animals during his lifetime so it wouldn't harm his serious reputation—making an exception only for 'The Swan.'

title: Gnossienne No. 1
stylisticClue: Exotic, modal F-minor melody with augmented-second twists floating without barlines.
funFact: Satie discarded bar lines and time signatures in this hypnotic piano piece, sprinkling the score with quirky French prompts like 'from the tip of thought.'

title: Children's Corner: Golliwogg's Cakewalk
stylisticClue: Syncopated cakewalk cake-strut winking mid-piece with a cheeky quote of Wagner's Tristan.
funFact: Written for his three-year-old daughter Chou-Chou, this ragtime-inspired piece playfully quotes Wagner's tragic opera Tristan and Isolde in the middle as a musical joke.

title: Ma mère l'Oye: Le Jardin féerique
stylisticClue: Hushed C-major strings rising into a shimmering, bell-drenched celesta and harp apotheosis.
spotifyQuery: Ravel Ma mere l'Oye Le Jardin feerique
funFact: Ravel originally composed Mother Goose as a four-hand piano duet for Mimi and Jean Godebski, the young children of his close friends Cipa and Ida.

title: Pavane in F-sharp minor
stylisticClue: Cool, poised solo flute tracing a wistful modal line over gentle pizzicato strings.
funFact: Fauré wrote this wistful, gently swaying dance in 1887 for an aristocratic patron, later adding an optional choir to give it a bittersweet Renaissance flair.

title: Préludes Book I: La cathédrale engloutie
stylisticClue: Hollow open fifths rising from the ocean depths into booming, bell-like organ sonorities.
funFact: Debussy's prelude brings to life a medieval Breton legend about the sunken city of Ys, whose cathedral rises above the waves only at sunrise.

title: Fountains of Rome: The Triton Fountain in the Morning
stylisticClue: Sparkling woodwind trills, celesta, and exuberant horn calls splashing in sunlight.
funFact: Respighi painted Rome's ornate Triton Fountain in sound using shimmering horns to mimic sea gods blowing conch shells, earning worldwide fame after Toscanini championed it.

title: Pomp and Circumstance March No. 1 (Trio)
stylisticClue: Broad, noble 'Land of Hope and Glory' string tune crowned by organ and brass.
spotifyQuery: Elgar Pomp and Circumstance March No 1
funFact: When King Edward VII heard this sweeping melody, he reportedly urged Elgar to add words to it—creating Britain's beloved anthem 'Land of Hope and Glory.'

title: Requiem: Pie Jesu
stylisticClue: Pure, luminous boy-soprano or soprano line floating over warm organ and muted strings.
funFact: Despite his mother dying weeks before its 1888 premiere, Fauré insisted he wrote this peaceful Requiem 'for pleasure,' viewing death as a gentle deliverance.

title: Peter and the Wolf: Peter's Theme
stylisticClue: Jaunty C-major string quartet theme skipping playfully with crisp classical clarity.
spotifyQuery: Prokofiev Peter and the Wolf Peter's Theme
funFact: Prokofiev wrote both the story and music for Peter and the Wolf in just two weeks to introduce Moscow schoolchildren to orchestral instruments.

title: Candide: Overture
stylisticClue: Brassy, asymmetric 2/2 and 3/2 fanfares racing into sparkling, witty Broadway-symphonic patter.
funFact: The 1956 Broadway musical Candide was a box-office flop that closed after 73 shows, yet its sparkling overture instantly became an orchestral concert favorite.

title: Masquerade Suite: Waltz
stylisticClue: Dark, swirling A-minor strings and brass sweeping forward with theatrical Soviet intensity.
funFact: Khachaturian struggled to write a worthy waltz for Lermontov's play Masquerade, which premiered on June 21, 1941—just one day before Germany invaded the Soviet Union.

title: Star Wars: Main Title
stylisticClue: Explosive B-flat brass fanfare and sweeping Korngold-inspired symphonic adventure theme.
spotifyQuery: John Williams Star Wars Main Title
funFact: George Lucas originally planned to score Star Wars with existing classical music, until friend Steven Spielberg urged him to hire John Williams instead.

title: Metamorphosis One
stylisticClue: Hypnotic, cycling E-minor broken triads shifting subtly between two-against-three pulses.
funFact: Philip Glass borrowed this haunting piano theme from his score for the 1988 crime documentary The Thin Blue Line, uniting it with Kafka's famous story.

title: Nuvole Bianche
stylisticClue: Gentle four-chord F-minor ostinato building steadily into cascading right-hand arpeggios.
funFact: Meaning 'White Clouds,' Einaudi composed this tranquil piece in 2004 after watching slow-moving clouds drift past the windows of his Milan apartment.

title: Spirited Away: One Summer's Day
stylisticClue: Quartal jazz-inflected piano chords opening into a nostalgic, bittersweet lyrical theme.
funFact: Joe Hisaishi wrote this nostalgic piano theme for Studio Ghibli's Spirited Away, capturing the bittersweet wonder of a young girl stumbling into a spirit world.

title: Rodeo: Hoe-Down
stylisticClue: Snappy orchestral square-dance fiddle tune punctuated by xylophone, woodblock, and brass.
funFact: For this lively cowboy dance, Copland adapted 'Bonaparte's Retreat,' a traditional American fiddle tune he learned from a 1937 Library of Congress field recording.

title: Concerto for Two Violins in D minor (I. Vivace)
stylisticClue: Two equal solo violins chasing each other in tight imitative counterpoint over driving continuo.
spotifyQuery: Bach Double Violin Concerto BWV 1043 Vivace
funFact: Bach wrote this energetic double concerto in Leipzig around 1730 for his student orchestra, later arranging it for a pair of solo harpsichords.

title: Solomon: Arrival of the Queen of Sheba
stylisticClue: Virtuosic twin oboes racing through joyful B-flat sixteenth-note flourishes against strings.
spotifyQuery: Handel Arrival of the Queen of Sheba
funFact: Handel wrote the entire three-hour oratorio Solomon in just over a month, opening its third act with this sparkling royal processional.

title: The Four Seasons: Autumn (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Hearty rustic harvest dance interrupted by tipsy, stumbling solo violin scale passages.
funFact: True to its accompanying poem, Vivaldi's 'Autumn' opens with joyful harvest dancing before portraying tipsy villagers stumbling and falling asleep.

title: Goldberg Variations: Aria
stylisticClue: Ornamented French sarabande melody unfolding over a stately, descending 32-measure bass line.
funFact: Legend claims Bach wrote these variations to soothe a sleepless Russian count, who supposedly rewarded the composer with a golden goblet full of coins.

title: Dido and Aeneas: When I Am Laid in Earth (Dido's Lament)
stylisticClue: Descending chromatic ground bass repeating eleven times beneath heartbroken soprano suspensions.
spotifyQuery: Purcell Dido's Lament When I am laid in earth
funFact: Purcell likely composed his only true opera for a girls' boarding school in Chelsea, ending it with Queen Dido's heartbreaking farewell before dying.

title: Harpsichord Concerto in F minor (II. Largo)
stylisticClue: Gentle pizzicato string pulse supporting an expressive, singing keyboard cantilena.
spotifyQuery: Bach Concerto in F minor BWV 1056 Largo
funFact: Bach helped invent the keyboard concerto by taking the harpsichord out of the background and giving it a starring solo role.

title: Oboe Concerto in D minor (II. Adagio)
stylisticClue: Poignant solo oboe ornamenting long, sighing Baroque phrases above steady pulsing strings.
spotifyQuery: Alessandro Marcello Oboe Concerto D minor Adagio
funFact: Johann Sebastian Bach admired this Venetian nobleman's oboe concerto so much that he arranged the entire piece for solo harpsichord.

title: Viola Concerto in G major (II. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Rich, warm solo viola leaping briskly through galant Baroque sequences and string tuttis.
spotifyQuery: Telemann Viola Concerto in G major Allegro
funFact: Telemann wrote the earliest known concerto for solo viola, giving an instrument usually stuck in the orchestra's middle a rare chance to shine.

title: Piano Concerto No. 5 'Emperor' (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Three massive E-flat orchestral chords each answered by sweeping, rhapsodic solo piano cadenzas.
spotifyQuery: Beethoven Piano Concerto No 5 Emperor Allegro
funFact: Beethoven drafted this heroic concerto in 1809 while Napoleon's troops shelled Vienna; a French officer's boast allegedly inspired the 'Emperor' nickname.

title: Don Giovanni: Overture
stylisticClue: Terrifying D-minor Statue chords and rushing scales pivoting abruptly into brisk, sparkling comedy.
funFact: Mozart famously stayed up all night before Don Giovanni's 1787 Prague premiere, finishing the overture's score just hours before the curtain rose.

title: Violin Concerto in D major (I. Allegro ma non troppo)
stylisticClue: Four quiet solo timpani taps launching a serene woodwind theme and radiant D-major poise.
funFact: This now-beloved concerto flopped at its 1806 premiere because the violinist had to sight-read Beethoven's freshly inked score right onstage.

title: Sinfonia Concertante in E-flat major (I. Allegro maestoso)
stylisticClue: Solo violin and scordatura viola trading noble phrases after a long orchestral Mannheim crescendo.
spotifyQuery: Mozart Sinfonia Concertante K 364 Allegro maestoso
funFact: To give the solo viola extra brilliance alongside the violin, Mozart asked the violist to tune all four strings slightly higher.

title: Symphony No. 6 'Pastoral' (I. Awakening of Cheerful Feelings)
stylisticClue: Drone fifths in low strings cradling a fresh, open-air F-major folk-like violin tune.
funFact: An avid nature walker, Beethoven wrote this countryside symphony alongside his Fifth, saying it expressed 'more the feeling than the painting' of nature.

title: Symphony No. 100 'Military' (II. Allegretto)
stylisticClue: Graceful French romance suddenly joined by triangle, cymbals, and booming bass drum.
funFact: Haydn thrilled London audiences by adding loud 'Turkish' percussion—triangle, cymbals, and bass drum—to paint the thrill and thunder of battle.

title: Piano Concerto No. 23 in A major (II. Adagio)
stylisticClue: Stark, intimate F-sharp minor siciliano opened by solo piano in hushed, tragic solitude.
spotifyQuery: Mozart Piano Concerto No 23 K 488 Adagio
funFact: Mozart wrote this concerto in 1786 while juggling rehearsals for The Marriage of Figaro, creating one of his most tender slow movements.

title: 26 Variations on La Folia di Spagna (or Sinfonia Veneziana)
stylisticClue: Crisp, theatrical Italian buffa strings and oboes bubbling with late-18th-century energy.
funFact: Despite movie myths of a bitter rivalry, Salieri actually mentored Mozart's son as well as young Beethoven, Schubert, and Liszt.

title: Violin Concerto in E minor (I. Allegro molto appassionato)
stylisticClue: Solo violin entering almost immediately with a passionate, singing E-minor melody over murmuring strings.
spotifyQuery: Mendelssohn Violin Concerto Op 64 Allegro molto appassionato
funFact: Mendelssohn worked on this concerto for six years with his close friend, violinist Ferdinand David, who advised him on every solo trick.

title: Piano Concerto in A minor (I. Allegro molto moderato)
stylisticClue: Dramatic timpani roll shattered by a thunderous, cascading A-minor piano octave descent.
spotifyQuery: Grieg Piano Concerto Op 16 Allegro molto moderato
funFact: A twenty-five-year-old Grieg wrote this dramatic concerto during a sunny Danish summer holiday, and it remains Norway's most famous classical export.

title: Piano Concerto No. 2 in C minor (I. Moderato)
stylisticClue: Eight tolling bell-like solo piano chords swelling into sweeping, surging C-minor strings.
funFact: After a disastrous symphony premiere left him depressed and unable to compose, Rachmaninoff recovered with hypnotherapy and dedicated this comeback concerto to his doctor.

title: Má vlast: Vltava (The Moldau)
stylisticClue: Two rippling flutes and clarinets merging into a sweeping, minor-to-major Bohemian river theme.
funFact: Although Smetana went completely deaf the year he composed this flowing river portrait, he could still 'hear' every orchestral ripple in his mind.

title: Pictures at an Exhibition: The Great Gate of Kiev
stylisticClue: Monumental Russian brass chorale alternating with tolling cathedral bells and swirling strings.
spotifyQuery: Mussorgsky Ravel Great Gate of Kiev
funFact: Mussorgsky wrote this grand finale after viewing his late friend Viktor Hartmann's architectural design for a ceremonial city gate that was never built.

title: Liebestraum No. 3 in A-flat major
stylisticClue: Warm baritone-register thumb melody wrapped in harp-like arpeggios and dazzling cadenzas.
funFact: Originally composed as a love song for voice and piano, Liszt later turned this tender melody into his most famous solo piano daydream.

title: Schwanengesang: Ständchen (Serenade)
stylisticClue: Gentle guitar-like staccato chords cradling a pleading, bittersweet D-minor melody.
funFact: Schubert wrote this aching serenade in the final months of his short life; it was published after his death in a collection called 'Swan Song.'

title: Violin Concerto in D major (I. Allegro moderato)
stylisticClue: Brief orchestral introduction leading to a radiant, singing D-major solo violin entrance.
spotifyQuery: Tchaikovsky Violin Concerto Op 35 Allegro moderato
funFact: Tchaikovsky's intended soloist rejected this concerto as 'unplayable,' and one harsh critic even claimed the music 'stank to the ear.'

title: Préludes Book I: La sérénade interrompue
stylisticClue: Plucked guitar-like piano grace notes repeatedly interrupted by distant, brisk fanfare fragments.
funFact: In this Spanish-flavored prelude, a lovestruck guitarist tries to play a serenade but keeps getting rudely interrupted by loud street noise.

title: Jeux d'eau
stylisticClue: Sparkling pentatonic and major-seventh water cascades shimmering across the upper keyboard.
funFact: Inspired by fountains and waterfalls, twenty-six-year-old Ravel dedicated this shimmering piano showcase to his composition teacher, Gabriel Fauré.

title: Pines of Rome (I. The Pines of Villa Borghese)
stylisticClue: Playful, glittering woodwinds, piano, and brass mimicking children's games in a sunny Roman park.
funFact: In this lively opening movement, Respighi uses playful orchestral melodies to imitate Roman children singing, marching, and playing war games beneath pine trees.

title: Villanelle for Horn and Piano
stylisticClue: Warm, hunting-horn echoing calls and stopped-horn colors over shimmering piano chords.
funFact: Written as a tough graduation exam piece for Paris Conservatory horn students, this rustic showpiece asks players to switch between modern and valveless horns.

title: Fantasia on a Theme by Thomas Tallis
stylisticClue: Resonant cathedral antiphony between full strings, distant muted echo choir, and solo quartet.
spotifyQuery: Vaughan Williams Fantasia on a Theme by Thomas Tallis
funFact: Borrowing a 1567 hymn tune by Tudor composer Thomas Tallis, Vaughan Williams premiered this lush string work inside Gloucester Cathedral in 1910.

title: Cello Concerto in E minor (I. Adagio — Moderato)
stylisticClue: Stark, declamatory solo cello quadruple-stops opening onto a wistful, rocking 9/8 theme.
spotifyQuery: Elgar Cello Concerto Op 85 Adagio Moderato
funFact: Haunted by World War I's devastation and his wife's failing health, Elgar poured his deepest sorrow into this autumnal, final major work.

title: The Planets: Mars, the Bringer of War
stylisticClue: Relentless 5/4 col legno string ostinato building into terrifying, dissonant brass fanfares.
funFact: Holst conceived this relentless, pounding war march just before World War I broke out in 1914, drawing inspiration from astrology rather than astronomy.

title: Images pour orchestre: Ibéria (III. Le matin d'un jour de fête)
stylisticClue: Distant marching bells and strummed guitar-like strings bursting into festive Spanish sunlight.
spotifyQuery: Debussy Iberia Le matin d'un jour de fete
funFact: Despite vividly capturing Spanish street festivals, bells, and guitars, Debussy had only ever set foot in Spain for a single afternoon at a bullfight.

title: Piano Concerto No. 3 in C major (I. Andante — Allegro)
stylisticClue: Wistful solo clarinet opening suddenly exploded by racing C-major string and piano scales.
funFact: Prokofiev premiered this dazzling concerto in Chicago in 1921, drawing on musical sketches he had saved in notebooks for nearly a decade.

title: Romanian Folk Dances
stylisticClue: Earthy modal violin tunes and crisp percussive rhythms straight from Transylvanian villages.
funFact: Bartók traveled rural villages with a heavy wax-cylinder phonograph, recording peasant fiddlers and turning their lively folk tunes into this colorful dance suite.

title: An American in Paris
stylisticClue: Jaunty walking theme punctuated by real Parisian taxi horns and a bluesy muted trumpet solo.
funFact: To capture bustling Parisian streets authentically, Gershwin actually bought four French taxi horns in Paris and brought them back for the orchestra to honk.

title: Petrushka: The Shrovetide Fair
stylisticClue: Bustling Russian carnival crowd music glittering with flute trills, accordion-like winds, and hurdy-gurdy.
funFact: This bustling opening scene sets a snowy Russian carnival where a street magician brings three puppets—including tragic Petrushka—magically to life.

title: The Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra (Theme)
stylisticClue: Noble Purcell hornpipe theme stated by full orchestra before passing section by section.
spotifyQuery: Britten Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra
funFact: Britten originally wrote this orchestral showcase for a 1946 educational film, letting every instrument family show off before uniting in a grand finale.

title: Libertango
stylisticClue: Propulsive 3-3-2 tango bass ostinato driving a fiery bandoneon and string melody.
funFact: Combining 'liberty' and 'tango,' Piazzolla recorded this electric hit in Milan in 1974 to signal his break from traditional Argentine dance-hall tango.

title: Short Ride in a Fast Machine
stylisticClue: Steadfast woodblock pulse propelling dazzling, shifting brass and synthesizer-like wind arpeggios.
spotifyQuery: John Adams Short Ride in a Fast Machine
funFact: Adams said this breathless, four-minute burst of orchestral energy captures the feeling of being talked into riding in someone's terrifyingly fast sports car.

title: Spiegel im Spiegel
stylisticClue: Slow, luminous F-major triadic piano arpeggios beneath long, pure ascending violin scales.
funFact: Written right before Pärt emigrated from Soviet Estonia, this tranquil, minimalist duet for violin and piano has become a modern favorite in films.

title: Brandenburg Concerto No. 4 in G major (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Two nimble recorders echoing and intertwining with a dazzlingly virtuosic solo violin.
funFact: Bach paired a dazzling solo violin with two wooden recorders—more often heard in gentle chamber music—giving them surprisingly athletic, showstopping parts.

title: L'estro armonico: Concerto for Two Violins in A minor (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Crisp unison A-minor ritornello launching interlocking solo violin sequences.
funFact: Known as 'The Red Priest' for his bright red hair, Vivaldi wrote many of his sparkling violin concertos for the talented orphaned girls he taught in Venice.

title: St. Matthew Passion: Erbarme dich, mein Gott
stylisticClue: Weeping solo violin obbligato sighing in B minor alongside a deeply expressive alto voice.
spotifyQuery: Bach St Matthew Passion Erbarme dich
funFact: After Bach's death, his St. Matthew Passion sat unperformed for decades until 20-year-old Felix Mendelssohn revived it in 1829, igniting the modern Bach revival.

title: Water Music Suite No. 1: Air
stylisticClue: Warm F-major string cantabile with poised oboe echoes floating gently over river breezes.
spotifyQuery: Handel Water Music Suite No 1 Air
funFact: King George I reportedly enjoyed Handel's Water Music so much during the 1717 Thames cruise that he ordered the musicians to play the whole program three times.

title: Violin Sonata in D minor 'La Folia'
stylisticClue: Solemn Spanish sarabande chord progression escalating into fiery solo violin bariolage.
funFact: Corelli built this fiery violin showpiece on 'La Folia,' a centuries-old Portuguese dance tune originally associated with wild, frenzied street celebrations.

title: Stabat Mater: Stabat Mater dolorosa
stylisticClue: Aching Baroque suspensions between soprano and alto weaving over walking F-minor strings.
funFact: Dying of tuberculosis at just 26, Pergolesi finished this deeply moving sacred masterpiece in a quiet Franciscan monastery only weeks before his death.

title: Harpsichord Concerto in D minor (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Relentless unison D-minor string theme driving fiercely virtuosic keyboard toccata episodes.
funFact: Bach helped invent the keyboard concerto by putting the harpsichord in the solo spotlight, often playing this dramatic piece himself at a Leipzig coffeehouse.

title: Tafelmusik: Concerto for 3 Trumpets in D major
stylisticClue: Three clarino trumpets trading brilliant fanfare imitation above crisp timpani and strings.
spotifyQuery: Telemann Concerto for 3 Trumpets TWV 54 D3
funFact: Telemann published Tafelmusik ('Table Music') by subscription to entertain wealthy diners at banquets, counting George Frideric Handel among his famous subscribers.

title: Symphony No. 4 in B-flat major (I. Adagio — Allegro vivace)
stylisticClue: Mysterious, shadowy B-flat minor introduction exploding into sunlit, effervescent B-flat joy.
funFact: Tucked between the stormy Third and Fifth symphonies, Beethoven's sunny Fourth was described by Robert Schumann as 'a slender Greek maiden between two Norse giants.'

title: String Quintet in G minor (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Dark, yearning G-minor upper strings answered by the rich, dusky warmth of paired violas.
funFact: Mozart wrote this darkly emotional string quintet weeks before his father died, adding a second viola to give the ensemble a richer, deeper voice.

title: Symphony No. 92 'Oxford' (I. Adagio — Allegro spiritoso)
stylisticClue: Off-tonic opening gesture launching one of Haydn's wittiest, most tightly spun sonata movements.
funFact: Written in 1789, this symphony earned its 'Oxford' nickname when Haydn conducted it there two years later to celebrate receiving an honorary doctorate.

title: Symphony No. 7 in A major (II. Allegretto)
stylisticClue: Hypnotic dactylic A-minor rhythm rising slowly from violas and cellos into monumental counterpoint.
funFact: This solemn, pulsing movement was such an instant hit at its 1813 charity premiere that the audience demanded an immediate encore mid-symphony.

title: Piano Concerto No. 17 in G major (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Bright, singing G-major violin melody with cheeky chromatic inflections and woodwind dialogue.
spotifyQuery: Mozart Piano Concerto No 17 K 453 Allegro
funFact: Mozart kept a pet starling that learned to whistle the finale's tune from this concerto, and he gave the bird a full funeral with poems when it died.

title: Médée: Overture
stylisticClue: Fierce F-minor unison slashes and Beethovenian storminess heralding tragic Greek drama.
funFact: Italian-born Cherubini conquered Paris during the French Revolution, and Beethoven admired his dramatic style so much that he called him the greatest living composer.

title: Piano Sonata No. 17 'Tempest' (III. Allegretto)
stylisticClue: Restless, galloping D-minor sixteenth-note perpetual motion driven by surging bass figures.
spotifyQuery: Beethoven Tempest Sonata Op 31 No 2 Allegretto
funFact: An unreliable early biographer claimed Beethoven said to 'read Shakespeare's The Tempest' to understand this stormy sonata, which he wrote while agonizing over his worsening deafness.

title: Trumpet Concerto in E-flat major (III. Rondo)
stylisticClue: Dazzlingly nimble classical trumpet leaping cleanly through sparkling rondo episodes.
funFact: Hummel wrote this cheerful concerto for a newly invented keyed trumpet in Vienna, helping transform the trumpet from a battlefield horn into a nimble solo instrument.

title: Symphony No. 6 'Pathétique' (I. Adagio — Allegro non troppo)
stylisticClue: Bleak solo bassoon emerging from double-bass gloom before explosive, Fate-driven passion.
funFact: Tchaikovsky considered this deeply personal symphony his finest creation; he conducted its premiere in St. Petersburg and died mysteriously just nine days later.

title: Symphony No. 3 'Scottish' (I. Andante con moto — Allegro)
stylisticClue: Misty A-minor wind and string ballad sweeping into stormy Highland seas.
funFact: Mendelssohn sketched the opening melody in 1829 after visiting the rain-swept ruins of Edinburgh's Holyrood Chapel, though it took him 13 years to finish the symphony.

title: Piano Concerto in A minor (I. Allegro affettuoso)
stylisticClue: Sharp orchestral chord and descending piano cascade opening onto a tender oboe romance.
spotifyQuery: Schumann Piano Concerto Op 54 Allegro affettuoso
funFact: Schumann wrote this passionate concerto for his wife, Clara—one of Europe's greatest pianists—who gave its triumphant Dresden premiere in December 1845.

title: Messa da Requiem: Dies Irae
stylisticClue: Four terrifying orchestral hammer-blows, thunderous bass drum, and swirling choral terror.
funFact: Opera master Verdi used thunderous chorus shouts and violent bass-drum blows to depict Judgment Day, making this sacred work as dramatic as any of his operas.

title: Scheherazade (I. The Sea and Sinbad's Ship)
stylisticClue: Stern brass sea-theme answered by a seductive, arabesque solo violin with harp.
spotifyQuery: Rimsky-Korsakov Scheherazade Sea and Sinbad's Ship
funFact: Before turning to music full-time, Rimsky-Korsakov served as a Russian naval officer, drawing on his own memories of ocean voyages for Sinbad's sea adventures.

title: Violin Concerto in D minor (I. Allegro moderato)
stylisticClue: Frosty muted violins shimmering beneath a rhapsodic, soaring D-minor solo violin.
funFact: Sibelius once dreamed of becoming a concert violinist; after stage fright ended that dream, he poured his lifelong love of the instrument into this fierce concerto.

title: Symphony in D minor (I. Lento — Allegro non troppo)
stylisticClue: Brooding chromatic three-note question rising from low strings into luminous organ-like brass.
spotifyQuery: Cesar Franck Symphony in D minor I
funFact: Organist César Franck completed his only symphony at age 65, though conservative Parisian critics initially scoffed at his unusual decision to include an English horn.

title: Symphony No. 2 in E minor (III. Adagio)
stylisticClue: Long, breathless solo clarinet cantabile spinning endlessly over lush, warm strings.
funFact: A decade after his First Symphony's disastrous premiere left him depressed for three years, Rachmaninoff proved his orchestral mastery with this lush, triumphant Second Symphony.

title: String Quartet in F major (II. Assez vif — Très rythmé)
stylisticClue: Cross-rhythmed pizzicato strumming punctuated by a soaring, lyric bowed cello and violin tune.
funFact: When Ravel's teacher suggested revising the quartet's finale, fellow composer Claude Debussy famously begged him: 'In the name of the gods of music, do not touch a single note!'

title: String Quartet in G minor (I. Animé et très décidé)
stylisticClue: Fierce Phrygian motto theme unifying sweeping French quartet textures and modal colors.
spotifyQuery: Debussy String Quartet Anime et tres decide
funFact: Debussy wrote only one string quartet, giving it the key and an official opus number—Opus 10—even though he avoided traditional numbering for nearly everything else.

title: La Péri: Fanfare
stylisticClue: Radiant French horns, trumpets, and trombones shimmering in rich whole-tone and ninth harmonies.
funFact: Perfectionist Paul Dukas burned most of his manuscripts before dying, sparing only a few works—including this blazing brass fanfare meant to quiet chatty ballet crowds.

title: Bacchus et Ariane Suite No. 2
stylisticClue: Pungent, muscular French orchestration driving ecstatic Dionysian rhythms and vivid brass.
spotifyQuery: Roussel Bacchus et Ariane Suite No 2
funFact: Like Rimsky-Korsakov, Albert Roussel spent seven years as a French naval officer sailing to Asia before switching careers to become a leading symphonic composer.

title: Tintagel
stylisticClue: Surging Atlantic string swells and glistening harp around a noble Cornish castle brass theme.
funFact: English composer Arnold Bax wrote this sweeping musical seascape after visiting the windswept cliffside ruins of Tintagel Castle, legendary birthplace of King Arthur.

title: The Sea: Seascape
stylisticClue: Luminous morning ocean shimmer with rolling harp arpeggios and sweeping English horns.
funFact: Future composer Benjamin Britten heard this ocean-inspired suite at age 10 and was so mesmerized by it that he went on to study with Frank Bridge.

title: The White Peacock
stylisticClue: Languid solo oboe floating over exotic, perfumed harmonic clouds and shimmering celesta.
funFact: American composer Charles Griffes wrote this dreamy piece while teaching piano at a New York boarding school, dying tragically at 35 months after its orchestral triumph.

title: Nocturnes (I. Nuages)
stylisticClue: Slowly drifting parallel clarinets and bassoons veiled by an unchanging English horn sigh.
funFact: Inspired by James McNeill Whistler's misty paintings, Debussy wrote 'Clouds' to capture the slow, quiet drifting of gray clouds across a Paris sky.

title: Music for Strings, Percussion and Celesta (III. Adagio)
stylisticClue: Eerie xylophone accelerando, timpani glissandi, and shivering celesta over dark divided strings.
spotifyQuery: Bartok Music for Strings Percussion and Celesta Adagio
funFact: Director Stanley Kubrick later used this eerie, sliding-string movement to chill audiences during the haunted hallway scenes of the horror classic The Shining.

title: Symphonic Metamorphosis on Themes of Weber (IV. March)
stylisticClue: Brassy, swaggering neo-Baroque march bursting with contrapuntal energy and crisp percussion.
funFact: After fleeing Nazi Germany for the United States, Hindemith transformed obscure four-hand piano pieces by 19th-century composer Carl Maria von Weber into an orchestral showpiece.

title: Symphony of Psalms (I. Exaudi orationem meam)
stylisticClue: Jagged E-minor orchestral stabs and churning double-reed ostinatos framing austere Latin chant.
funFact: Composed 'to the glory of God' for the Boston Symphony's 50th anniversary, Stravinsky omitted all violins and violas to give the orchestra an ancient, solemn sound.

title: Violin Concerto (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Soaring, warm G-major solo violin entering immediately without an orchestral introduction.
spotifyQuery: Samuel Barber Violin Concerto Op 14 Allegro
funFact: Commissioned by a wealthy soap magnate for his protégé, the piece was rejected by the young violinist, who claimed the opening was too simple and the finale unplayable.

title: Symphony No. 4 (I. Poco moderato — Poco allegro)
stylisticClue: Sunlit, syncopated piano-and-string rhythms swirling with buoyant Moravian neo-Baroque energy.
funFact: Czech composer Bohuslav Martinů wrote this radiant, joyful symphony in America during the final weeks of World War II as Allied victory finally came into sight.

title: Viola Concerto (I. Andante comodo)
stylisticClue: Wistful, syncopated A-minor solo viola spinning bittersweet Gershwin-meets-Elgar lyricism.
spotifyQuery: William Walton Viola Concerto Andante comodo
funFact: Walton wrote this soulful concerto for top English violist Lionel Tertis, who turned it down—leaving fellow composer Paul Hindemith to triumph at the 1929 premiere.

title: Musica Ricercata: VII. Cantabile, molto legato
stylisticClue: Perpetual left-hand folk ostinato beneath a serene, singing right-hand melody built on limited pitches.
funFact: Ligeti built Musica Ricercata as a strict musical puzzle, adding one new note per piece and limiting this gentle seventh movement to just eight different notes.

title: Music for 18 Musicians (Pulses)
stylisticClue: Pulsing marimbas, pianos, and breath-length clarinets cycling through eleven shifting chords.
spotifyQuery: Steve Reich Music for 18 Musicians Pulses
funFact: With no conductor leading them, the 18 musicians cue each new section using gentle chimes and the natural length of a human breath on the bass clarinet.

title: Concerto for Oboe and Violin in C minor (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Crisp C-minor unison ritornello launching tightly woven dialogue between oboe and violin.
spotifyQuery: Bach Concerto for Oboe and Violin BWV 1060 Allegro
funFact: Bach's original score for this lively double concerto is lost; today's beloved version for oboe and violin was reconstructed from his arrangement for two harpsichords.

title: Dixit Dominus: Dixit Dominus
stylisticClue: Blazing G-minor string moto perpetuo driving explosive five-part choral counterpoint.
funFact: A fiery 22-year-old Handel wrote this explosive choral work while visiting Rome, driving singers through relentless, breathless energy that still pushes choirs to their limits.

title: Praeludium in C major
stylisticClue: Thundering pedal solo opening into bright manual fugues and a rolling ground-bass chaconne.
spotifyQuery: Buxtehude Praeludium in C major BuxWV 137
funFact: Buxtehude's thrilling organ showpieces made him a legend in northern Germany; in 1705, a 20-year-old Bach famously walked over 250 miles just to hear him play.

title: Platée: Overture
stylisticClue: Dotted French-overture majesty giving way to croaking, witty Baroque woodwind comedy.
funFact: Written for a royal wedding at Versailles, Rameau's satirical comedy stars a vain swamp frog tricked into believing Jupiter loves her—a risky joke about the bride's looks.

title: L'estro armonico: Concerto Grosso in D minor (I. Allegro — Largo)
stylisticClue: Interlocking solo violins and cello building a fiery Baroque fugue over driving continuo.
spotifyQuery: Vivaldi Concerto Grosso Op 3 No 11 RV 565
funFact: Published in 1711, Vivaldi's L'estro armonico became a European sensation; J.S. Bach admired this fiery D-minor concerto so much that he arranged it for solo organ.

title: Magnificat in D major: Magnificat anima mea
stylisticClue: Jubilant D-major Baroque trumpets and swirling woodwind runs launching five-part chorus.
funFact: Bach first wrote this radiant Magnificat for his debut Christmas in Leipzig with extra festive hymns tucked inside, before polishing it into this brighter version later.

title: Pièces de clavecin: Les Barricades Mystérieuses
stylisticClue: Hypnotic lutenist style brisé arpeggios interlocking smoothly across overlapping keyboard voices.
funFact: Scholars still debate what 'The Mysterious Barricades' means—from eyelashes or corsets to wine barrels—making this hypnotic harpsichord gem one of music's favorite riddles.

title: Sinfonia in D major (or Corelli Sonata)
stylisticClue: Antiphonal interplay between a delicate concertino trio and full Baroque string ripieno.
funFact: When Stradella premiered his oratorio San Giovanni Battista in Rome in 1675, a 22-year-old Arcangelo Corelli played violin in the orchestra and absorbed his bold style.

title: Piano Sonata No. 32 in C minor (II. Arietta)
stylisticClue: Hushed C-major hymn transforming through accelerating subdivisions into proto-boogie-woogie.
spotifyQuery: Beethoven Piano Sonata No 32 Op 111 Arietta
funFact: In his very last piano sonata, a nearly deaf Beethoven wrote a set of variations whose wildly bouncing rhythm sounds startlingly like early jazz or ragtime.

title: Piano Concerto No. 20 in D minor (I. Allegro)
stylisticClue: Restless syncopated strings and ominous double-bass rumblings before a pleading solo piano entry.
spotifyQuery: Mozart Piano Concerto No 20 K 466 Allegro
funFact: Mozart finished this stormy, dramatic concerto the day before its 1785 premiere with the ink barely dry, creating a dark favorite of both Beethoven and Brahms.

title: The Creation: Representation of Chaos
stylisticClue: Shocking, tonally unmoored C-minor unison and shifting chromatic sighs resolving into light.
spotifyQuery: Haydn The Creation Representation of Chaos
funFact: Inspired by hearing Handel's grand choral works in London, Haydn opened The Creation with eerie, unsettled chaos before a blinding burst proclaims 'Let there be light!'

title: Violin Sonata No. 9 'Kreutzer' (I. Adagio — Presto)
stylisticClue: Solo violin quadruple-stops in A major shifting to A minor before a furious presto duel.
funFact: Beethoven wrote this ferocious sonata for mixed-race virtuoso George Bridgetower, then rededicated it to Rodolphe Kreutzer—who refused to play it—after a quarrel over a woman.
